title: Machine Learning Models for Predicting Sea Surface Temperature Variability and Trends
abstract: Sea Surface Temperature (SST) is an important factor in understanding climate systems, weather patterns, and marine environments. Accurate prediction of SST helps in forecasting events like cyclones, monsoons, and climate change impacts. Traditional methods often fail to capture complex and nonlinear patterns present in SST data. In this research, machine learning models such as Linear Regression, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) are used to predict SST variability and trends. Historical SST datasets from satellite and climate sources are used for training and testing the models. The performance of each model is evaluated using standard metrics like Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and R² score. The results show that LSTM performs better than other models due to its ability to learn time-based patterns effectively. This study proves that machine learning can significantly improve SST prediction accuracy and can be useful for climate-related applications.
field: Machine learning for sea surface temperature prediction
problem: Traditional methods for predicting Sea Surface Temperature (SST) have low long-term forecasting accuracy because they fail to capture the complex, nonlinear patterns and long-term dependencies inherent in large, dynamic ocean datasets.
method: The paper proposes applying and comparing multiple machine learning models, including Linear Regression, Random Forest, and LSTM, on historical datasets to predict Sea Surface Temperature (SST) variability and trends and identify the best-performing model.
task: The task is to predict Sea Surface Temperature (SST) variability and trends by applying and comparing various machine learning models, including LSTM and Random Forest, on historical SST datasets to find the most effective model.
innovation: This study comparatively evaluates several machine learning models for predicting Sea Surface Temperature, demonstrating that the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model achieves the highest accuracy by effectively capturing long-term temporal dependencies in historical data.
